rejected.why: 止 itself is シ and lends no sound — the real phonetic in 政 整 症 証 is the larger unit 正, 歳 takes its sound from 戌/戉, and 企 歩 歯 歴 use 止 as the foot radical for meaning.
Duplicate of the accepted 生 = セイ series; ショウ is merely the go-on layer of the same phonetic, and shipping both would give the learner two competing cards for one fact.
Duplicate of the accepted 者 = ショ series — same component and same transmission, just the minority reading layer; merged into one card so 著/緒/暑/都 are not taught twice with contradictory keys.
𠂇 is the drawn left hand used for meaning, not a sound carrier — 右 有 友 agree because those Old Chinese hand-words were near-homophones themselves, and 左 サ and 布 フ show the shape predicts nothing.
A stroke fragment from the decomposition, not a real shared component — 無 and 舞 match because 舞 is the original graph of 無 itself, while 午 毎 旅 族 監 share only a slanted top stroke.
𠂇 is the hand pictograph used for meaning, not sound — 友 右 有 rhyme because they are a cognate word family, and the same element yields サ in 左 and フ in 布.
㐅 is a bare X-stroke artifact: the shape inside 気 descends from the 米 of 氣 and the one in 希 from 爻, so there is no shared component to transmit a sound.
丷 is a two-stroke fragment rather than a component — it also caps 半 平 弟 金 商 楽 with six unrelated readings, so リツ in 立 率 is pure coincidence.
卌 is a stroke-grid artifact; 無 and 舞 do share ブ, but only because both descend from the same plumed-dancer pictograph, not because any 卌 element carries sound.
The 卜 in 下 is just a downward-pointing indicator stroke, unrelated to the divination crack in 外, and ゲ is merely the go-on reading the two happen to share.
